paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God wants you to KNOW how much Christ loves you, and He gives you the strength to take it in. Paul asks the Father to strengthen the saints "with power through His Spirit in your inner being, so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith" (Ephesians 3:16-17). Notice that Paul starts on the inside, not with an easier life. The love of Christ isn't something you earn by being impressive. It's something you get rooted in, like a tree that doesn't have to prove anything to the dirt (Ephesians 3:17).

Now here's the part that gets me. Paul says the love of Christ has "length and width and height and depth," and that it "surpasses knowledge" (Ephesians 3:18-19). So you will never reach the edge of it, and that's the good news! He also says you grasp it "together with all the saints," so you don't have to go it alone (Ephesians 3:18). Your hands are full of it, and so are the hands of the believer sitting next to you.

And Paul ends by looking up. God is able to do "immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine, according to His power that is at work within us" (Ephesians 3:20). So go ahead and pray big, baker, because you could never out-ask Him. The glory belongs to Him "in the church and in Christ Jesus throughout all generations, forever and ever. Amen" (Ephesians 3:21). That's a love worth being rooted in, and a God worth every bit of your praise.
